observation.visible_scene: A wide view of a large waterfall gorge under an overcast, cloud-streaked sky. A tall, dense column of white spray/mist rises from the left and center of the frame, largely hiding the cliff face behind it. On the right, a broad sheet of water cascades over the cliff edge, with tan/brown-tinted water visible along the top rim. Foreground tree branches and leaves frame the top edge and the bottom-right corner, and a thin branch arcs in from the left.
visible_changes: The mist column continuously billows and churns: its internal density, the dark patches within it, and its soft edges fluctuate from frame to frame, while it remains a vertical column occupying the left-center throughout (no onset or completion).
The right-side cascade shows ongoing flow: the white foam streaks and the texture of the falling water shift over time, and the tan water at the top rim moves downward along the edge.
Foreground vegetation, the horizon line, and the right cliff edge stay in fixed screen positions across all frames, so the apparent motion is from the water and mist, not from the camera.
No editing cut or seam is visible; the sequence reads as one continuous shot.
outside_clip_unknowns: What happens to the spray column before or after this ~2.7 s window (whether it grows, shrinks, or clears) is not shown.
The impact zone at the base of the falls that generates the mist is below/behind the visible spray and is not seen.
The exact flow rate or source of the waterfall is unknown.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain, but the unchanged framing of background and foreground suggests the camera is essentially stationary (no clear pan/zoom).
Minor apparent drift of the mist's left boundary is most consistent with turbulence rather than lateral translation of the whole column.
